name: Evil Twin / Rogue AP
description: An evil twin attack creates a wireless access point that mimics a legitimate network, tricking clients into connecting to the attacker's infrastructure. Once connected, traffic can be intercepted, credentials harvested, and clients served malicious content. The Wi-Fi Pineapple automates much of this attack surface and is the standard tool for this technique. The Enterprise version is recommended for walkthrough assessments in large multi-floor environments due to its superior range.

blue.det: WIDS detects rogue AP or evil twin inside facility; clients connecting to unknown BSSID; endpoint alert on connection to unrecognized network.
blue.cm: WPA3 Enterprise with certificate-based authentication; WIDS deployed inside facility; 802.1X preventing credential capture from wireless; network segmentation limiting blast radius of captured credentials.
